text: {"overall_winner":"A","qualities":[{"evidence":"clear claim that driverless cars \"should be developed\"","quality":"clear thesis","description":"The essay states its position directly and early so the reader knows exactly what it is arguing."},{"evidence":"three organized body paragraphs on efficiency, safety, and convenience","quality":"organizational structure","description":"The essay develops its argument in a clear, purposeful sequence of points instead of moving randomly from idea to idea."},{"evidence":"repeated references to article details like Sergey Brin, sensors, GM, Tesla, and 2020 plans","quality":"textual support","description":"The essay grounds its claims in multiple specific details from the source rather than relying mainly on general statements."},{"evidence":"explains fuel use, CO2, safety sensors, and taxi flexibility","quality":"development of reasoning","description":"The essay connects evidence to broader claims with clearer explanation of why the details matter."},{"evidence":"ending that contrasts \"human-driven cars\" with \"driverless cars\"","quality":"conclusion","description":"The essay closes by restating its position in a memorable way and bringing the argument to a finish."}]}
